genre_name: Methods / system paper describing an AI research agent and its validation (benchmarks, ablations, case studies)
scope: Original research papers that introduce an LLM-based (or otherwise AI) research agent or multi-agent system for science, describe its architecture and tools, and validate it with benchmarks against baselines, component ablations, case studies or discoveries (sometimes with wet-lab confirmation), human or LLM-judge evaluation, cost/runtime and safety analysis. This is the genre of Amani's own system paper (PW11). Not covered: benchmark-only papers that evaluate other agents, reviews/perspectives, clinical decision-support or diagnostic agents, and single-model tools without an agentic loop.
word_count_convention: jats_structure.py prose words; captions/tables/citations/headings excluded; main = I+M+R+D(+L,C); for this genre also counts E2's headed safety sections ('other') and E3's Experimental Section as Methods

standard_items.text: The system still makes errors: incorrect implementations, hallucinated facts or citations, failed runs; failure modes are characterised
Validated only on a narrow set of domains, tasks, input types or computational-only experiments; generalisation untested
Benchmark coverage and evaluation validity are limited: small or self-built test sets, task-selection bias, subjective expert or LLM scoring, missing ablations
Dual-use or misuse risk remains despite built-in safeguards; societal risks (e.g. flooding peer review) acknowledged
Performance depends on the specific (often proprietary) LLM backbone and version; other or newer models not fully tested
Not fully autonomous: humans still run experiments, approve steps or correct the agent (semi-autonomous)
Discoveries validated only at an early stage (in vitro, workshop-level review, predicted properties) or not experimentally validated
Output quality depends on compute budget or run length; longer runs not explored

variation_notes: House style drives most structural variation. Nature Portfolio (6/9: E1, E2, E4, E5, E6, E7) uses an untitled lead instead of an 'Introduction' heading, declarative Results subheadings, online Methods last, Extended Data figures (4 of 6), a one-sentence web summary and, where life-science content exists, a Reporting Summary. Nature 2026 (E6) replaces the Discussion with a top-level Limitations section; Nature 2023 (E1) has no main-text Methods. Wiley Advanced Materials (E3) merges Results and Discussion, adds a long Conclusion and puts the 'Experimental Section' last, with many figures (12) and tables (5) and no baselines. Cell Press Patterns (E8) adds Highlights, The bigger picture and an eTOC blurb and gathers declarations in a 'Resource availability' block with a lead contact. OUP Bioinformatics (E9, ISMB proceedings) is numbered IMRaD with Conclusions, a structured abstract that carries the code URL, and the fewest references (33). Design also matters: discovery systems with wet-lab confirmation (E1, E2, E5, E7) carry experimental methods, validation panels and Reporting Summaries; computational systems (E4, E6, E8, E9) put more weight on benchmark tables, repeated runs, ablations and cost. Code release depends on dual-use concern (withheld in E1, E5).
lint_notes: Figure 1 must be the system architecture/workflow schematic (9/9). For Amani: the plan -> worker -> kernel -> gates -> label pipeline, with human (owner) touchpoints marked.

Every quantitative claim of improvement needs a named baseline and run-to-run variation (n runs or raters plus s.d./s.e.m./CI) in the text or caption (8/9). Flag 'outperforms' without a comparator or without n.

The Methods must name every LLM (worker, judge, rater). Amani should go past the exemplars: exact version string, provider, access dates and knowledge cutoff (TRIPOD-LLM style); only 3/9 exemplars give version strings and 0/9 give access dates.
Code availability must state its release status in words (open with licence / partial / withheld with reason). Garmin IP check before release (design section 11.5).
A limitations passage is required even when unheaded (8/9): look for a paragraph with limitation cues in the closing section; Amani's protected Part A/Part B limitations satisfy this.
A safety/dual-use paragraph is typical (6/9). For a biomedical agent that ranks drugs or targets, treat it as required.
If any human rated outputs (owner, experts, reviewers), require an ethics/consent statement; exemplars are inconsistent here (2/6).

Map Amani's evidence to the genre's slots: benchmark_comparison = calibration (V3) and known-answer suite results vs a no-gate baseline; ablation_plot = gate-removed comparisons; error_taxonomy = defects found by K-acc re-probes and false-Confirmed cases; validation_panel = reproduction of published results; cost_table = runtime and compute per project.
Results subsection headings in Nature-style venues are declarative claims ('X outperforms Y in Z'); Amani's claim-wording lint should apply to headings too.

Abstract: one unstructured paragraph of 100-250 words naming the system, its components, the evaluation scope (with counts) and one concrete demonstration; structured only if the venue demands it (Bioinformatics: Motivation / Results / Availability and implementation).
Agent transcripts or example outputs must be released somewhere (8/9): supplement, repository or Zenodo bundle.
notes: Contamination exclusions (structure looked suitable, excluded because Amani's topics appear in the body): Co-Scientist (Gottweis et al., Nature 2026, PMC13345910) uses an ALS mechanism goal as its running worked example; AutoBA (Adv Sci 2024, PMC11600294) uses mouse pancreatic-islet RNA-seq as its worked example; Biomni (bioRxiv 2025, PMC12157518; peer-reviewed version Science 2026, 10.1126/science.adz4351, not open access) has an embryonic hip/knee/shoulder joint multi-omics case study; Kosmos (arXiv 2511.02824) includes a pancreatic-islet type 2 diabetes discovery. contamination_title_abstract is empty for all nine chosen exemplars; body scans are empty too.

Other candidates not used: Virtual Lab (Nature 2025) is not open access (bioRxiv only); data-to-paper (NEJM AI 2025) is not open access and its arXiv version has no HTML; BioDiscoveryAgent (ICLR 2025) not needed given 9 peer-reviewed journal exemplars. LLM-RDF (Nat Commun 2024) and SciToolAgent-type tool papers were considered.

All nine exemplars are peer-reviewed journal articles: 6 Nature Portfolio (E1, E2, E4, E5, E6, E7), 1 Wiley (E3), 1 Cell Press (E8) and 1 OUP (E9, an ISMB 2026 proceedings paper in Bioinformatics). There is no preprint exemplar; PW11 will be posted as a preprint, which imposes no structure, so the Nature-style layout is the target.
E4's Extended Data case example uses a KEGG neurodegeneration gene set (not ALS-specific); contamination scans are empty.
Year = issue year (E3 online Dec 2024, issue 2025; E5 online Jul 2025, issue 2026).
Section words for unheaded intro/results splits (E1, E7) come from subtraction within the tool's section tree; limitations words for unheaded passages are estimates.
Nature formatting guidance quoted in notes was read from nature.com on 2026-10-13. Caps for Patterns, Advanced Materials and Bioinformatics were not checked; the venue profiles should hold them.

New display-item ids not in the shared vocabulary: safety_guardrail_example, agent_prompt_figure, algorithm_box. Kinds seen once only (network_plot E3, volcano_plot E7 panel, composition_bar E9, glossary_box E4) are left out of display_items.
Ablation and failure analysis counts depend on what is counted (strict component removal vs any comparison); the frequency strings give both.
